preamble: Nasalization of the close-mid back vowel [o] to [õ]. It arises from assimilation to an adjacent nasal: Old French had nasalized [õ] before any nasal consonant (bon [bõn], bone [bõnə]); in Portuguese the nasal consonant after o was then absorbed, leaving phonemic õ in bom and som; in Paraguayan Guaraní nasal harmony spreads nasality from a stressed nasal syllable across the word, nasalizing oral /o/.

examples.note: Via Old Galician-Portuguese bõo; the nasal consonant was absorbed into the vowel.
Nasal vowels were allophones of oral vowels before a nasal consonant, which was still pronounced (Modern French [bɔ̃]).
Nasalization applied in open syllables too; Modern French bonne [bɔn] later denasalized.
Nasality of the stressed syllable spreads leftward, nasalizing each /o/.

languageExamples.context: Nasal harmony spreading leftward from a nasal stressed syllable
